Use the afternoon to find onboarding obstacles. Five participants cannot reliably establish which version has the higher completion rate. A completion-rate winner is **Not verified**.

The current phase is evaluation planning: recommend a test and a decision rule, without running research or changing either version.

1. **Define completion first.** Specify the same meaningful end event and observation window for both versions. Count all eligible onboarding starters in the denominator, including those who abandon. The current completion rate and smallest improvement worth shipping are Unknown.
2. **Check recruitment.** Twelve active users per week does not mean twelve new onboarding users. Seek five people who match the intended audience and have not already learned the flow. If only experienced users are available, label their feedback accordingly.
3. **Run five short diagnostic sessions.** Allow 30 minutes for preparation, five 20-minute sessions, and 30 minutes for synthesis. Randomly assign three people to one version and two to the other. Give everyone the same realistic goal, starting conditions, and neutral instructions. Observe an initial attempt without coaching; record completion, abandonment point, errors, time, and requests for help. Discuss confusion afterward. Each person sees one version, avoiding practice effects.
4. **Make a provisional product decision.** Summarize observed obstacles and their consequences, with participant counts and concrete examples. Do not turn a 3/3 versus 1/2 result into a population-level winner. If one version reveals a serious blocker, recommend fixing it or provisionally choosing the other. If findings are mixed, retain the current version pending stronger evidence. Label any choice as a usability-informed judgment.
5. **Measure completion later if the comparison still matters.** Randomly assign eligible new users 50/50, keep assignment stable, and use the agreed completion definition. Set the minimum worthwhile lift, sample requirement, and stopping rule before starting, using a measured baseline. Report uncertainty and allow an inconclusive result; do not stop at the first favorable result.

Even if all twelve weekly users were eligible new starters, that gives only about six per version per week. Actual traffic may be lower, so a credible rate comparison could take substantial time. The feasible afternoon deliverable is a short obstacle report and a provisional recommendation, not proof of a higher completion rate.
